statement.summary: Lemma 3.3 is one paper sentence with six claims, frozen as six Props: `torsionEqStatement` (𝒜[p] = ((n/p)ℤ/nℤ)^d as sets), `torsionIsoStatement` (the formula x = (n/p)y ↦ y mod p determines `torsionCoord`, and `torsionCoord` restricted to 𝒜[p] is an additive isomorphism onto 𝔽_p^d), `torsionOrderStatement` (order-p elements ↔ nonzero vectors), `torsionLinesStatement` (C ↦ lineOf C is a bijection 𝓛_p → lines, compatible with the isomorphism), `torsionCountStatement` (|𝓛_p| = [d 1]_p and = (p^d−1)/(p−1), in ℚ) and `torsionJoinStatement` (|⟨⋃J⟩| = p^{rk J}). `torsionLemmaStatement` is their conjunction.
deltas: Standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1 (Definition 2.1); 'Let p ∣ n be prime' = `p.Prime → p ∣ n`. No alphabet appears.
p𝐱 = `p • x` (ℕ-scalar multiplication on `Fin d → ZMod n`); 𝒜[p] = `latTorsion n d p`, whose carrier is literally `{v | p • v = 0}`.
((n/p)ℤ/nℤ)^d is rendered as the set of x whose every coordinate is the residue of some integer (n/p)·y; n/p is ℕ-division, exact since p ∣ n.

The paper's map 𝐱 = (n/p)𝐲 ↦ 𝐲 mod p is realised by `torsionCoord` (canonical representative val(x_i)/(n/p)); that it agrees with y mod p for EVERY integer representation x = (n/p)y is the first conjunct of `torsionIsoStatement`.
'Isomorphism of 𝔽_p-vector spaces' is an `AddEquiv` 𝒜[p] ≃+ (Fin d → ZMod p): 𝒜[p] has no ZMod p-module instance; additive maps between 𝔽_p-spaces are automatically 𝔽_p-linear, so nothing is lost.

'Correspond' is made concrete: order-p elements lie in 𝒜[p] and have order p iff their image is nonzero; C ↦ lineOf C (𝔽_p-span of the image of C ∩ 𝒜[p]) is a `Set.BijOn` from 𝓛_p onto the finrank-1 submodules, and x ∈ C ↔ torsionCoord x ∈ lineOf C on 𝒜[p].
𝓛_p = `orderPCyc n d p` (cyclic: C = zmultiples g for some g; order p: Nat.card C = p).
The count is stated in ℚ, against the paper's product definition `gaussProd` of [d 1]_p and against (p^d−1)/(p−1) separately (chain a = b = c as a = b ∧ a = c).
rk J = finrank of ⨆_{C∈J} lineOf C (the span of the lines = their join); J is any subset of 𝓛_p, J = ∅ included.

maps.label: p ∣ n prime
maps.note: Every one of the six Props carries both hypotheses.

maps.label: standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1
maps.note: From Definition 2.1; the lemma involves no alphabet, so no σ hypothesis.

maps.label: 𝒜[p] = ((n/p)ℤ/nℤ)^d

lean.text:
{x : Lat n d | p • x = 0}
      = {x : Lat n d | ∀ i, ∃ y : ℤ, x i = ((((n / p : ℕ) : ℤ) * y : ℤ) : ZMod n)}

maps.note: Equality of subsets of 𝒜 = `Lat n d`.

maps.label: 𝒜[p] = {x : px = 0}
maps.note: In the equality Prop the torsion is written as the set itself; the other Props use the subgroup `latTorsion n d p` with this carrier (or the hypothesis `p • x = 0`).

maps.label: ((n/p)ℤ/nℤ)^d

lean.text: {x : Lat n d | ∀ i, ∃ y : ℤ, x i = ((((n / p : ℕ) : ℤ) * y : ℤ) : ZMod n)}

maps.note: (n/p)ℤ/nℤ ≤ ℤ/nℤ as the residues of the integers (n/p)·y; the d-th power is 'for every coordinate i'.

maps.label: n/p
maps.note: ℕ-division, exact because p ∣ n is a hypothesis; then cast to ℤ.

maps.label: the map 𝐱 = (n/p)𝐲 ↦ 𝐲 mod p

lean.text:
(∀ (x : Lat n d) (y : Fin d → ℤ),
        (∀ i, x i = ((((n / p : ℕ) : ℤ) * y i : ℤ) : ZMod n)) →
          torsionCoord n p d x = fun i => ((y i : ℤ) : ZMod p))
fun i => (((x i).val / (n / p) : ℕ) : ZMod p)

maps.note: `torsionCoord` uses the canonical representative y_i = val(x_i)/(n/p); the first conjunct says it equals y mod p for every integer y with x = (n/p)·y, i.e. the paper's formula is well defined and is this map.

maps.label: isomorphism 𝒜[p] ≅ 𝔽_p^d of 𝔽_p-vector spaces

lean.text:
∃ e : latTorsion n d p ≃+ (Fin d → ZMod p),
      ∀ x : latTorsion n d p, e x = torsionCoord n p d (x : Lat n d)

maps.note: An additive isomorphism whose underlying function is the paper's map (not merely some isomorphism). ≃+ instead of ≃ₗ: every additive map between 𝔽_p-vector spaces is 𝔽_p-linear.

maps.label: 𝔽_p^d
maps.note: 𝔽_p = `ZMod p` (a field since p is prime); 𝔽_p^d = functions Fin d → ZMod p.

maps.label: elements of order p ↔ nonzero vectors

tex.text: elements of order $p$ correspond to nonzero vectors

lean.text:
(∀ x : Lat n d, addOrderOf x = p → p • x = 0) ∧
    (∀ x : Lat n d, p • x = 0 → (addOrderOf x = p ↔ torsionCoord n p d x ≠ 0))

maps.note: Every order-p element lies in 𝒜[p], and on 𝒜[p] order p ⟺ nonzero image; together with the bijection of (b) this is the correspondence.

maps.label: elements of order p
maps.note: Order = `addOrderOf` in 𝒜 (equal to the order in the subgroup 𝒜[p]).

maps.label: nonzero vectors
maps.note: Image under the map of (b) is nonzero.

maps.label: 'Under it' (correspondence via the isomorphism)

lean.text:
∀ C ∈ orderPCyc n d p,
      (∀ x ∈ C, p • x = 0) ∧
      ∀ x : Lat n d, p • x = 0 → (x ∈ C ↔ torsionCoord n p d x ∈ lineOf n d p C)

maps.note: Makes the line correspondence 'under' the isomorphism: each C ∈ 𝓛_p lies in 𝒜[p] and its image under torsionCoord is exactly lineOf C (no abstract equinumerosity).

maps.label: cyclic subgroups of order p ↔ lines

tex.text: cyclic subgroups of order $p$ correspond to lines

lean.text:
Set.BijOn (lineOf n d p) (orderPCyc n d p)
        {W : Submodule (ZMod p) (Fin d → ZMod p) | Module.finrank (ZMod p) W = 1}

maps.note: Bijection = `Set.BijOn` (maps 𝓛_p into lines, injective on 𝓛_p, onto all lines).

maps.label: cyclic subgroups of order p (𝓛_p)

lean.text: {C | (∃ g : Lat n d, C = AddSubgroup.zmultiples g) ∧ Nat.card C = p}

maps.note: 'Cyclic' literally as C = ⟨g⟩, 'order p' as |C| = p. (Named 𝓛_p only in Lemma 3.4.)

maps.label: lines of 𝔽_p^d

lean.text: {W : Submodule (ZMod p) (Fin d → ZMod p) | Module.finrank (ZMod p) W = 1}

maps.note: Lines = 1-dimensional 𝔽_p-subspaces (finrank 1).

maps.label: the line corresponding to C

lean.text: Submodule.span (ZMod p) (torsionCoord n p d '' {x : Lat n d | p • x = 0 ∧ x ∈ C})

maps.note: 𝔽_p-span of the image of C ∩ 𝒜[p] under the map of (b); that this image already is the line is the 'under it' conjunct.

maps.label: their number is [d 1]_p = (p^d−1)/(p−1)

lean.text:
(Nat.card (orderPCyc n d p) : ℚ) = gaussProd p d 1 ∧
    (Nat.card (orderPCyc n d p) : ℚ) = ((p : ℚ) ^ d - 1) / ((p : ℚ) - 1)

maps.note: The chain |𝓛_p| = [d 1]_p = (p^d−1)/(p−1) as two equalities with common left side, in ℚ.

maps.label: their number |𝓛_p|
maps.note: `Nat.card` of the (finite) set 𝓛_p, cast to ℚ.

maps.label: [d 1]_p (paper's product formula)
maps.note: The Gaussian binomial exactly as the §3 preamble defines it (product over i < r, integer exponent d − i via zpow, in ℚ) — not the project's recursive `gaussBinom`.

maps.label: (p^d−1)/(p−1)
maps.note: Rational division, so no ℕ truncation is possible.

maps.label: |⟨⋃J⟩| = p^{rk J} for J ⊆ 𝓛_p

tex.text:
for a set $J$ of
order-$p$ cyclic subgroups

lean.text:
∀ J : Set (AddSubgroup (Lat n d)), J ⊆ orderPCyc n d p →
      Nat.card (AddSubgroup.closure (⋃ C ∈ J, (C : Set (Lat n d)))) = p ^ rk n d p J

maps.note: J an arbitrary set of order-p cyclic subgroups (automatically finite); J = ∅ included (1 = p^0).

maps.label: a set J of order-p cyclic subgroups

tex.text: for a set $J$ of order-$p$ cyclic subgroups

lean.text: ∀ J : Set (AddSubgroup (Lat n d)), J ⊆ orderPCyc n d p →

maps.note: J ⊆ 𝓛_p.

maps.label: |⟨⋃J⟩|

lean.text: Nat.card (AddSubgroup.closure (⋃ C ∈ J, (C : Set (Lat n d))))

maps.note: Cardinality of the generated subgroup.

maps.label: ⟨⋃J⟩

lean.text: AddSubgroup.closure (⋃ C ∈ J, (C : Set (Lat n d)))

maps.note: The subgroup generated by the union of the carriers.

maps.label: p^{rk J}

lean.text: p ^ rk n d p J

maps.note: Natural-number power.

maps.label: rk J = dim of the span of the corresponding lines

tex.text: $\rk J$ is the dimension of the span of the corresponding lines

lean.text: Module.finrank (ZMod p) ↥(⨆ C ∈ J, lineOf n d p C)

maps.note: The span of a family of subspaces is their join ⨆; dimension = `Module.finrank`; the lines are `lineOf C` as in (d).
